title: Crystallize: a two-minute reasoning game about evidence, calibration and replication (SYNTHETIC)
description: SYNTHETIC educational game, zero dependencies, offline, English and French. The player decides how much synthetic data to reveal before claiming that a hidden direction exists in noisy 2-D readings, states a probability scored by the Brier rule (a strictly proper scoring rule), and faces a simulated reviewer's replication. Includes a daily seeded puzzle, a plain-text share card, challenge links in the URL hash, streaks kept in local storage only, and an exact Bayesian reference observer for the generator. No accounts, no network calls. Not clinical, no real patients or data.
